cards.text: This one's a Maskil of David, from after Doeg the Edomite, one of Saul's servants (1 Samuel 21:7), went to King Saul and told him, “David has gone to the house of Ahimelech.” Ahimelech was a priest (1 Samuel 21:1). David opens this psalm with a question for a mighty man, and friend, it's the kind of question your boss asks when he ALREADY knows the answer.

cards.question: David asks the mighty man why he's bragging. What does David say the mighty man boasts of?

cards.text: Then, right next to all that bragging, David slides in one quiet line about God. The mighty man brought a megaphone, and David brought the line that's STILL going after the megaphone's batteries die.

cards.question: Right after his question to the mighty man, David says the ___ of God endures all day long.

cards.text: Then David zooms in on the man's mouth and calls him a worker of deceit. His tongue devises destruction like a sharpened razor, and friend, that tongue needs a WARNING LABEL.

cards.question: David compares the mighty man's tongue to a sharpened razor. What is that picture saying about his words?

answers.text: They cut and do real harm
They sound wise but mean nothing

cards.text: And it gets worse: David says this man loves evil more than good. That's a man who walks up to a tray of fresh cookies and picks the burnt one ON PURPOSE.

cards.question: David says the mighty man loves speaking truth more than falsehood.

cards.text: After a Selah, David comes RIGHT back at that tongue like a man who thought of his best comeback in the shower. He calls it a deceitful tongue that loves every word that devours.

cards.question: David says the mighty man's deceitful tongue loves every word that devours. What kind of words are those?

cards.text: Now the psalm turns from what the mighty man does to what God will do about it. And friend, the mighty man has done ALL the talking so far, so that's about to change.

cards.question: What does David say God will surely do to the mighty man?

answers.text: Bring him down to everlasting ruin
Give him time to change his ways
Make him pay back what he took

cards.question: David says God will snatch the mighty man up and tear him away from his tent.

cards.text: And God will uproot him from the land of the living. After a Selah, David pictures the righteous seeing it: they fear, and they mock the evildoer.

The righteous point at the fallen man and say exactly where it went wrong: he leaned on the wrong thing. Friend, I spent years in a drawer leaning on dead batteries that SWORE they still had a charge, so I am in no position to judge.

cards.question: The righteous say the man didn't make God his refuge. What did he trust instead?
The righteous say the fallen man strengthened himself by helping others.

cards.text: Then David flips it with two little words, “But I,” and now he's talking about himself. He pictures himself as an olive tree in the house of God.

cards.question: The mighty man gets uprooted from the land of the living. But David says he is like an olive tree ___ in the house of God.
Unlike the man who trusted his wealth, David says he trusts in the loving devotion of God forever and ever.

cards.text: And David closes with a promise to praise God forever. No end date, no snooze button, no “let me get back to you after the holidays,” just FOREVER.

cards.question: Why does David say he will praise God forever?
David says he will wait on God's name, because it is good. Where will he wait?

answers.text: In the presence of God's saints
In the court of King Saul
